findings: The overview remains a domestic NZD, reusable, delayed bank debit for NZ accounts and customers, with approval and extra identity verification after an access request. New customer-flow text explicitly identifies a submitted debit as pending processing and separates it from final success or failure. SetupIntent creates the mandate, and the documented retrieval follows SetupIntent.mandate to GET /v1/mandates/{id}. Checkout and Payment Element collect terms acceptance, while any non-Stripe-hosted collection must present the terms and confirm acceptance. A customer may cancel via bank or business. Detach the PaymentMethod to inactivate the associated Stripe mandate and collect a new DDA before new authorized debits. mandate.updated can also mark it inactive after permanent failure (old raw lines 75-85, 121-133; new raw lines 140-170 and 265-281).

Refund handling now distinguishes a pre-submission request that cancels the payment from a post-submission request that remains pending until payment success. The latter is described as failed if the debit fails. Retrieve the Refund to track it. May said a refund requested before completion starts at PaymentIntent succeeded and is marked canceled if PaymentIntent enters requires_payment_method (old raw lines 183-193; new raw lines 96-122). Preserve both dated states and avoid treating the old canceled and new failed descriptions as interchangeable API outcomes.

May called it private preview, November drops the label but does not establish GA (old raw lines 195-197; new raw lines 257-263).

November adds statement descriptor precedence and 12-character truncation, then account business name and Stripe as fallback. Direct charges use the connected account. contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-nz-becs-debit-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-nz-becs-debit.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account documents a reusable, delayed domestic NZD bank debit for approved NZ accounts and customers with NZ bank accounts. It covers NZ-based merchants and Connect platforms or marketplaces serving NZ customers in B2B or B2C, for domestic payments only. Access requires approval and additional identity verification. Businesses with prohibited merchant category codes (MCCs) cannot use the method. A business with a restricted MCC may be able to use it and must provide additional information when creating the account (new raw lines 29-45). The separate business-category list identifies additional prohibited or restricted categories (new raw lines 309-324). The NZD 0.50 minimum and NZD 999,999,999.99 scheme ceiling are separate from the default NZD 10,000 per-transaction limit and initial NZD 10,000 weekly volume limit. Payments must satisfy both actual account limits, which can differ by approval status and subsequent increases. A customer Direct Debit Authority must authorize Stripe to debit (new raw lines 9-16, 18-69 and 309-324). Checkout and Payment Element collect terms acceptance. Other collection paths require displaying the terms and confirming acceptance. A SetupIntent can identify the mandate, and detaching the PaymentMethod inactivates the Stripe mandate after cancellation. Customer debit submission takes place before final payment success or failure. Standard success and balance availability are T+2 business days from submission at 00:00 UTC, with an 18:20 Pacific/Auckland cutoff and an estimated Charge debit date (new raw lines 140-170, 210-222 and 265-281). The overview supports recurring payments and saving via Payment Intents or Setup Intents yet marks off-session payments unsupported. The separate November acceptance and setup guides document later server off_session=true PaymentIntents using attached payment methods, so the support boundary remains unresolved (new raw lines 172-208). The May overview establishes the same DDA, domestic NZD, delayed payment, standard timing, support-assisted email override and dispute/refund basics (old raw lines 8-73 and 109-193). source-stripe-nz-becs-debit.md preserves many of those details but omits November's precise scope and conflates the debit notice deadline with Stripe's send trigger and dispute creation with balance removal.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account, substantive November documentation changes include the approval and account-versus-scheme limit detail, explicit UI/product/API exclusions, mandate retrieval/inactivation, new pre-submission cancellation and post-submission Refund tracking, retry limits, and Connect descriptor rules (new raw lines 14-69, 87-122, 140-196 and 257-301). Reordered sections, table layout, replacement of illustrations and guide links are presentational or navigational. The revised flow's distinction between submission and final success is meaningful (old raw lines 75-107 and new raw lines 197-208 and 265-281). In source-stripe-nz-becs-debit.md keep May's day-of-debit requirement, private-preview label and failed-payment refund described as canceled dated (old raw lines 135-167 and 183-197). November says no later than debit day, describes Stripe's separate immediate pre-debit send after successful confirmation, and says a post-submission pending refund is failed if the debit fails (new raw lines 96-106 and 224-255). Preserve the separate dated mandate sample wording. The May overview says within five days of establishing the mandate (old raw lines 135-143), while the May acceptance and setup samples say no later than five business days after the customer confirms the DDA (acceptance lines 244-257 and setup lines 200-212). The November overview and both November samples use five days (new raw lines 224-245, November acceptance lines 215-232 and November setup lines 211-224). Add reciprocal warnings for this earlier discrepancy to the overview, acceptance, setup and concept routes. The mandate confirmation window is separate from the per-debit notice deadline and Stripe's immediate pre-debit send after successful PaymentIntent confirmation. The May overview describes up to two business days from debit initiation to receive a result (old raw lines 8-12). The November overview's standard settlement table shows payment success and availability in the Stripe balance at T+2 from submission at 00:00 UTC (new raw lines 210-222). The separate November acceptance guide lines 275-289 describes notification of the PaymentIntent's success or failure within three business days after Stripe submits the debit. Keep these time bases and outcomes explicit on both linked routes. A dispute-created event and a bank ruling that triggers fund removal are distinct. The 9-month and 120-day windows have separate starting dates (old raw lines 169-181 and new raw lines 124-138). Add reciprocal warnings across the overview, acceptance, setup, NZ BECS concept and index. The November overview flags off-session payments as unsupported despite listed future-use and recurring capabilities (new raw lines 172-208). The separately dated November acceptance guide lines 291-320 and setup guide lines 259-296 show a new server PaymentIntent with confirm=true and off_session=true after a PaymentMethod attaches to a customer-configured Account or Customer. The older guides show dated Customers v1 examples. A saved or recurring payment method, an accepted request and a submitted debit establish distinct states. The documentation conflict provides no general off-session availability or payment-success conclusion.
